# @aponiajs/openapi

> Serve an OpenAPI document for an Aponia application's routes, with the document's own metadata read from a validated configuration. A thin adapter over `@elysia/openapi`: AponiaJS contributes a module the plugin is declared in and a validated configuration the document's `title`, `version`, and `description` come from, and no generator of its own.

**This package does not validate requests, does not generate clients, and serves no interface of its own.** The document is a *description* of the routes the platform compiled, not a contract the server enforces: nothing here makes a request conform to what the document says, and a client generated from the document is a third-party generator's reading of it, with that generator's own gaps. The only interface served is the wrapped plugin's, at the mount path — Scalar's page by default. A reader who assumes enforcement will ship a client for endpoints that answer `422`, or an integration against a route that was never declared.

**A reader who wants the raw plugin should use [`@elysia/openapi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@elysia/openapi) directly.** Nothing here is unavailable there, and mounting it through an Aponia `PluginModule` costs a few lines. What this package adds is declaration through a module and validation of the document's metadata, and nothing else.

## What this package exports

```ts
import { OpenApiModule } from "@aponiajs/openapi";
import type { OpenApiConfiguration, OpenApiInfo, OpenApiModuleOptions } from "@aponiajs/openapi";
```

- `OpenApiModule` — `OpenApiModule.register(options)` returns the `DynamicModule` an application's `imports` accepts.
- `OpenApiConfiguration` — `{ info }`, the value the module validates and exports.
- `OpenApiInfo` — `{ title, version, description? }`. `title` and `version` are required because OpenAPI requires them; an absent `description` is served as no description rather than as the plugin's `"Development documentation"` placeholder.
- `OpenApiModuleOptions` — `configuration`, `source`, `key`, and `path`.

## Declaring a document

```ts
import { Module } from "@aponiajs/common";
import { OpenApiModule } from "@aponiajs/openapi";
import { OpenApiConfig } from "./config.ts";

const docs = OpenApiModule.register({ configuration: OpenApiConfig });

@Module({ imports: [docs], controllers: [WidgetsController] })
export class AppModule {}
```

The document is served at `"/openapi/json"` and the interface at `"/openapi"`, both moved together by `path`. `key` defaults to `"openapi"`, and two registrations sharing one are refused as `DUPLICATE_MODULE`. A `path` that is not absolute is a `TypeError` raised while the registration runs.

`aponia build` declines a module whose `imports` name a registration — a registration is not a `@Module()` class, so no spelling of the call keeps the module lowerable — and the application still boots and serves the document by lowering the root from its decorators.

## What the document reflects

What the platform lowered from the route decorations, and nothing else: the path and method of each route, `requestBody` from a declared `body`, `parameters` from `query`, `params`, `headers`, and `cookie`, and `responses` from a declared `response` — one validator as the `200` answer, a status map as the status-specific answers. A route with no schema is still an operation.

Two absences to know: `components.schemas` is empty, because AponiaJS registers no model and every declared schema is inlined into the operation that declared it; and a WebSocket gateway is not in the document, because the platform mounts it as a route whose method is `ws`, which is not an OpenAPI path-item field — the plugin is mounted with `exclude.methods: ["options", "ws"]` for that reason. `operationId`, `summary`, `tags`, `security`, and `servers` are not populated: the framework declares none of them.

## One document per application

Elysia mounts a *named* plugin once, and this plugin is named. Two registrations with distinct keys produce two graph nodes and one document — whichever mounted first — while the second path answers `404` and reading the shared configuration token back raises `AMBIGUOUS_PROVIDER`. One registration per application is the supported shape.

## Errors

`AponiaError` with `INVALID_CONFIGURATION_VALUE`, carrying `{ configuration, issues }`, when the schema rejects the value or the value it produced is not an `{ info }` object with a non-empty `title` and `version`. The issue list is total: every field that fails is reported at once. `INVALID_CONFIGURATION` covers a declaration that is not a Standard Schema or whose validation answers asynchronously.
